thread:
nina-recruiter: Hi all — new hire (Priya K) accepted offer for SWE IC role, start date May 3. She's still in India renewing her passport and likely won't have it back until mid-May. She asked if she can start remotely from India as Redwood W-2 or if we should push start date. Thoughts?

emma-peopleops: Short: we can't onboard someone as US W-2 if they will be working physically from India unless we have a local entity or a contractor arrangement. We need to decide: 1) defer start date; 2) hire as contractor via local EOR/vendor; or 3) allow unpaid/voluntary onboarding (docs + trainings) until authorized.

santiago-hiring-manager: Candidate can start doing onboarding work and code reviews — we want them onboard earlier if possible. What about starting as an independent contractor for 2-3 weeks?

anya-legal: We can't convert an employee offer into W-2 retroactively if they work abroad without employer-side payroll setup. Risk: local employment law and tax nexus in India, plus misclassification risk. Options: 
- Use our EOR partner (Velocity/Remote) to engage them as a local contractor/employee for short term.
- Defer official start date until passport done and they can travel.
- Offer a short-term contractor SOW (via EOR or third-party) for "onboarding services"; ensure no change to the original offer terms except start date and note benefits won't apply while on contractor status.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: if using EOR, submit EOR request form and budget code. Also attach candidate signed SOW to the hiring ticket.

karen-payroll: Benefits/Payroll implications: 
- If they remain contractor (EOR), Redwood benefits (medical, 401k) don't apply.
- If we defer start, benefits effective date tied to first W-2 payroll. Open enrollment/eligibility windows still apply based on payroll effective date.
- We need a payroll cost delta estimate (EOR fees ~10-25%+ local taxes). I can run numbers if you pick EOR route.

nina-recruiter: Candidate prefers to start earlier if possible. She can sign a contractor SOW and prefers EOR. She asked whether sign-on bonus or relocation would be affected.

emma-peopleops: Good question — policy: sign-on and relocation are tied to W-2 employment. If we onboard via EOR for <90 days then convert to W-2, we can make sign-on contingent on completing conversion and pro-rate relocation. Need policy confirmation from comp/people ops.

anya-legal: Draft language we usually use: "Candidate will be engaged via [EOR] as a short-term local employment contractor until Redwood can onboard the candidate as a Redwood U.S. employee pending completion of passport/visa/work authorization. All offer elements that depend on U.S. employment (medical, 401k, relocation stipend, sign-on bonus) will be paid following conversion to Redwood W-2, subject to policy." I'll prepare a one-pager and SOW template.

santiago-hiring-manager: If we do EOR, how long to set up? Candidate needs to start around May 3.

karen-payroll: EOR setup for a candidate usually is 3-5 business days if we have candidate docs (passport scan, local address, bank details) and budget approvals. If vendor needs contract, add 2 days. If we need to approve EOR fees >$1k, loop in finance.

emma-peopleops: Action items: 
- @nina-recruiter: confirm candidate ok with EOR and collect ID + bank info; confirm willingness to sign SOW.
- @anya-legal: draft SOW + conditional offer amendment language; include clause about benefits and sign-on timing.
- @karen-payroll: provide EOR cost estimate and timeline; confirm payroll effective date upon conversion.
- I'll queue a tentative deferred start date (May 24) in the offer system in case EOR can't be in place.

nina-recruiter: Candidate confirmed willing to use EOR for short term. Uploading docs now. She asked if Redwood will cover EOR fees.

emma-peopleops: We typically cover reasonable EOR fees for short-term bridging for critical hires; pre-approving up to $1,500 for a 30-day bridge. If estimate higher, escalate to finance. Tag hiring cost center when submitting.

anya-legal: Uploaded a draft SOW template to the hiring ticket and will DM a redline. Key point: explicit statement that contractor period doesn't alter original offer and conversion timeline.

karen-payroll: Running numbers now — will post estimate (EOR fee + employer local taxes) in 2 hours.

santiago-hiring-manager: Thanks — please keep this thread concise. If EOR works, start them right away. If not, we'll push to May 24.

emma-peopleops: Perfect. Keep receipts/contract for expense reimbursement. Closing notes: do not complete I-9 until candidate physically in US and authorized to work; for now collect I-9 docs copies for intake only.

people-ops-bot: Checklist: EOR request submitted? /eor request -> attach candidate docs, SOW, budget code.

nina-recruiter: Uploaded docs and candidate signed SOW. Thanks everyone — will update when payroll estimate is in.

karen-payroll: Estimate posted: EOR fees ~$1,200 + local employer contributions ~8% => total ~ $1,296 for 30 days. Within pre-approval.

emma-peopleops: Approved. Proceed with EOR onboarding and mark the official Redwood W-2 start date as conversion date (to be updated once passport/authorization confirmed).

santiago-hiring-manager: Awesome, thanks team :rocket:
